$comment: External data-flow inventory for Netzar OS Enterprise. This file is the SOURCE OF TRUTH for docs/security-model.md: every processor outside the deployed AWS account (plus the Bedrock prompt path, which stays inside AWS but matters for model-privacy questions) gets an entry here. If you add code that sends data anywhere new, add an entry here in the same PR. Fields: id (stable slug), processor (who receives the data), dataCategories (what leaves), direction (outbound | inbound | bidirectional), when (the condition under which the flow is active), optOut (how an operator turns it off), status (active | provisioned-unused | planned), notes (code pointers and caveats).

dataCategories: bot tokens in API call headers
flows.when: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN (or a per-agent Slack connection) is configured and the slack_posting kill switch is off
flows.optOut: Do not connect Slack; or trip the slack_posting kill switch to stop outbound posts
flows.notes: src/adapters/slack/handler.ts (inbound events, HMAC-verified), src/adapters/slack/send.ts and src/adapters/slack/multi-agent.ts (two outbound send paths: main bot and per-agent apps)

dataCategories: voice notes, photos, and PDFs (downloaded from Telegram's file API, then stored in your S3)
agent replies, optional Polly voice replies
bot tokens in API call URLs
flows.when: TELEGRAM_TOKENS_JSON is configured and the telegram_posting kill switch is off
flows.optOut: Do not connect Telegram; or trip the telegram_posting kill switch to stop outbound posts
flows.notes: src/adapters/telegram/handler.ts (inbound webhook, secret-token verified), src/adapters/telegram/send.ts and media.ts (outbound replies, media download)

flows.processor: Amazon Bedrock (AWS service, inside your account boundary; cross-region inference profiles route to their destination AWS regions)
dataCategories: full prompts: agent system prompt, injected memories, hive notes, inbox items, conversation history, user message
flows.when: Every agent turn; this is the core function of the system
flows.optOut: No opt-out while serving traffic; the bedrock_global kill switch halts all model calls. Per AWS's service terms, Bedrock does not use your inputs or outputs to train models
flows.notes: src/agent/agent-loop.ts (ConverseStream + Converse), src/lib/bedrock/client.ts. The configured guardrail is attached to every call unless guardrail_disabled or a per-turn skip (War Room) applies

flows.when: TAVILY_API_KEY is set, the web_search tool is invoked, and web_search_disabled is off
flows.optOut: Unset the key; trip web_search_disabled; or set CCE_WEB_SEARCH_PII_POLICY=refuse
flows.notes: src/lib/search/adapters/tavily.ts via src/lib/tools/web-search-tools.ts. The outbound query passes a PII gate (CCE_WEB_SEARCH_PII_POLICY: refuse | redact (default) | allow) before leaving

flows.when: BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY is set, web_search is invoked, and web_search_disabled is off
flows.optOut: Unset the key; trip web_search_disabled; or set CCE_WEB_SEARCH_PII_POLICY=refuse
flows.notes: src/lib/search/adapters/brave.ts. The adapter dispatcher picks the first configured vendor (Tavily, then Brave, then Exa, then Serper)

flows.when: EXA_API_KEY is set, web_search is invoked, and web_search_disabled is off
flows.optOut: Unset the key; trip web_search_disabled; or set CCE_WEB_SEARCH_PII_POLICY=refuse

flows.when: SERPER_API_KEY is set, web_search is invoked, and web_search_disabled is off
flows.optOut: Unset the key; trip web_search_disabled; or set CCE_WEB_SEARCH_PII_POLICY=refuse

dataCategories: none today; the API key is provisioned but no runtime code calls Google
flows.when: Never in the current codebase. GOOGLE_GEMINI_API_KEY is plumbed through the vendor-keys secret into the task env (infra/lib/compute-stack.ts, src/config/env.ts) for planned Gemini-backed features, but src/ has no consumer
flows.optOut: Leave GOOGLE_GEMINI_API_KEY unset; with no key and no caller, no data can flow
flows.notes: Listed so the provisioned key is not invisible. If a Gemini consumer lands, this entry must be updated to active in the same PR

flows.processor: Operator-configured MCP servers (AgentCore gateways inside AWS, or vendor-hosted remote MCP endpoints such as mcp.slack.com)
dataCategories: tool call arguments (model-generated, can contain conversation content)
tool results (flow back into the model context)
flows.when: One or more servers are registered in runtime-config (category mcp, key servers), the server is enabled for the agent, and the tool_use / tool_dispatch_disabled kill switches are off
flows.optOut: Remove or disable the server in the Integrations tab; or trip tool_use to detach all tools
flows.notes: src/lib/mcp/servers-repo.ts (registry, HTTPS-only, iam | bearer | none auth), src/lib/mcp/client.ts (SigV4 for AgentCore, bearer for vendors), dispatched from src/agent/agent-loop.ts. Which processors are involved depends entirely on which servers the operator registers

flows.processor: The customer-selected Salesforce tenant and Salesforce APIs
dataCategories: OAuth client credentials and access/refresh tokens
SOQL query text and query results
record identifiers and fields read, created, updated, or deleted
flows.when: An administrator configures and authorizes the Salesforce connection, a Salesforce tool is invoked, and salesforce_disabled is off
flows.optOut: Do not connect Salesforce; disconnect/remove its OAuth configuration; or trip salesforce_disabled
flows.notes: src/lib/oauth/providers.ts performs customer-configurable login/token exchange and refresh; src/lib/salesforce/client.ts and src/lib/tools/salesforce-tools.ts send queries/records to the instance_url returned by Salesforce. PGN does not proxy this flow

flows.processor: Amazon SES, delivering to arbitrary external recipients
flows.when: CCE_EMAIL_FROM is set with a verified SES sender, the send_email tool is invoked, and email_send_disabled is off
flows.notes: src/lib/tools/email-tools.ts. SES itself is AWS-native, but the delivered mail leaves your boundary to whoever the recipient is; recipient and body caps apply

dataCategories: egress IP of the build machine
flows.when: Every image build: npm ci inside the Docker build (Dockerfile), local deploys, and CodeBuild builds (buildspec.yml)
flows.optOut: Point npm at a private registry mirror; there is no in-app toggle because this is build-time, not runtime
flows.notes: Build-time only. The running Fargate task does not call npm

flows.processor: Public container registries (Docker Hub / Amazon ECR Public) serving base images
dataCategories: egress IP of the build machine
flows.when: Every image build (Dockerfile base-image pull, docker buildx in deploy.ts and buildspec.yml)
flows.optOut: Mirror base images into your private ECR and point the Dockerfile at the mirror
flows.notes: Main application and Paperclip artifacts are built/imported into private ECR, but this entry is build-time only. The separately listed runtime-sidecar flow covers public X-Ray and optional Cloudflare image references

flows.processor: Amazon ECR Public and public Cloudflare container distribution
dataCategories: customer NAT/egress IP and pull timing
flows.when: A task starts with the public AWS X-Ray daemon image or an enabled Cloudflare sidecar that has not been mirrored into customer ECR
flows.optOut: Mirror every approved sidecar by digest into customer ECR and reference only the private copy
flows.notes: infra/lib/compute-stack.ts defines the X-Ray and optional cloudflared containers. This is software-distribution metadata, not application payload, but it is an external runtime dependency and must be captured in the release SBOM

flows.processor: GitHub (github.com), via the account-level CodeBuild source credential
dataCategories: a GitHub PAT stored as an account-level AWS CodeBuild source credential
flows.when: CCE_CODEBUILD_ENABLED=1 and the operator has run aws codebuild import-source-credentials; builds trigger on deploy tags
flows.optOut: Keep CCE_CODEBUILD_ENABLED off; deploy from your laptop with npm run deploy instead
flows.notes: infra/lib/codebuild-stack.ts, buildspec.yml. The credential is account-wide AWS state (it outlives the stack); the ci-coherence doctor check and the teardown catalog both know about it

flows.processor: Cloudflare and the PGN-controlled pgnos.ai zone
dataCategories: complete encrypted browser HTTP and WebSocket traffic in transit
request/response metadata, hostnames, IP addresses, headers, cookies, and payloads visible according to the Cloudflare service configuration
flows.when: CCE_PUBLIC_ACCESS=1 enables the PGN-only infra-only overlay for app.pgnos.ai or staging.pgnos.ai
flows.optOut: Required for customer production: leave CCE_PUBLIC_ACCESS unset and configure DOMAIN_NAME/CCE_DASHBOARD_URL plus customer-owned DNS/TLS
flows.notes: infra/lib/public-dashboard-access.ts deliberately restricts this mode to pgnos.ai and makes it mutually exclusive with DOMAIN_NAME. It is PGN demo/staging infrastructure, never the customer-production path

dataCategories: none in the Netzer task configuration; both upstream opt-out flags are set to the exact value 1
flows.when: Not active in Netzer-managed ECS or the integration harness; would be possible only if an operator removes both opt-out controls or changes the upstream component
flows.optOut: PAPERCLIP_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 and DO_NOT_TRACK=1 are hardcoded in infra/lib/paperclip-stack.ts and docker-compose.paperclip.yml
flows.notes: The pinned upstream Paperclip line defaults anonymized telemetry on. Netzer disables it explicitly so customer workloads do not call home by omission; infra/lib/paperclip-stack.test.ts asserts both flags

dataCategories: CI logs and artifacts (test output, cdk synth output) stored on GitHub infrastructure
with CCE_CICD_ENABLED=1, OIDC-federated deploy actions run against your AWS account from GitHub runners
flows.when: The repo's workflows run (ci.yml on pushes/PRs, cdk-drift.yml daily, deploy.yml when CI deploys are enabled)
flows.optOut: Disable Actions on your fork, or keep CCE_CICD_ENABLED off so no workflow holds AWS deploy authority
flows.notes: .github/workflows/. The drift workflow assumes an OIDC role (CDK_DIFF_ROLE_ARN secret) and reads repo Variables for domain and model ids; treat workflow logs as public-ish on a public repo

dataCategories: egress IP and timing of the install's daily releases check; no payload telemetry
flows.when: The dashboard checks the public GitHub releases feed, backend-side and fail-silent, cached daily (src/lib/updates/discovery.ts, wired via src/adapters/dashboard/handler.ts)
flows.optOut: CCE_UPDATE_CHECK_DISABLED=1 (implemented; short-circuits with zero network calls); air-gapped installs lose only the update banner
flows.notes: Implemented but not commercially usable because the current repository has no releases or populated signing trust roots. src/lib/updates/discovery.ts now defaults to Adams-Captial-Holdings-Ltd/Netzer-Labs; CCE_UPSTREAM_OWNER/CCE_UPSTREAM_REPO can override it. The call remains backend-side, cached, and fail-silent
